id: 351-猶太人反對君士坦丁烏斯·加盧斯的起義
theater: 巴勒斯坦行省提比哩亞與凱撒利亞

battle.name: 猶太人反對君士坦丁烏斯·加盧斯的起義
battle.theater: 巴勒斯坦行省提比哩亞與凱撒利亞
battle.brief: 公元351年，羅馬帝國內戰抽走巴勒斯坦的駐軍，提比哩亞的猶太人在拉比朱利安·本·薩巴率領下起事，奪取兵械、毀掉凱撒利亞市場上的皇帝像，353年前後被平定。卡面埃及月牙劍是青銅時代的單刃鉤形砍刀，標示近身一擊不回抽的纏鬥邏輯。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 這場起義的交戰雙方，是羅馬帝國君士坦丁王朝治下的巴勒斯坦行省，與提比哩亞、加利利湖岸一帶的猶太社群；它不是國家之間的戰爭，而是一次發生在帝國內戰縫隙裡的行省叛亂。羅馬一方以皇帝君士坦丁烏斯二世為最高權力來源，由駐節凱撒利亞的行省總督坐鎮，下轄提比哩亞的駐軍堡壘、稅吏與後備兵；東部的帝國軍隊主力卻在351年全年被抽調西去，鎮壓的力量因此空虛。起義一方並非獨立政權，而是以拉比階層為核心的提比哩亞猶太市民：城中的拉比學院與公議會、稅務登記官、銀匠與農人，在駐軍薄弱的空隙裡武裝起來。背景是羅馬帝國第一次全面內戰——西部的軍隊在高盧與不列顛推舉馬格嫩提烏斯為帝，與君士坦丁烏斯二世爭奪皇位；巴勒斯坦名義上仍效忠君士坦丁烏斯二世，卻被捲進兩方的拉鋸。整場衝突沒有第三國介入，也沒有外邦援助，這是四世紀巴勒斯坦猶太人最後一次以整座城市為基地的武裝起事。
countriesEn: The two sides in this rising were the Roman province of Palaestina under the Constantinian dynasty on one hand, and the Jewish communities of Tiberias and the shore of the Sea of Galilee on the other; it was not a war between states but an armed rebellion inside a province that opened up in the gap of an imperial civil war. On the Roman side the supreme authority was the emperor Constantius II, with the provincial governor resident at Caesarea and beneath him the garrison fortress at Tiberias, the tax collectors and the reserve soldiers; yet the main body of the imperial army in the East was drawn away westward throughout the year 351, and the strength available for repression was hollow. The insurgents were no independent state, but the Jewish townsmen of Tiberias organised around the rabbinic class: the rabbinic academy and the council of the town, the registrars of the tax, the silversmiths and the peasants, who armed themselves in the gap left by the thin garrison. The setting was the first empire-wide civil war of the Roman state, in which the troops of the West proclaimed Magnentius emperor in Gaul and Britain and fought Constantius II for the throne; Palaestina nominally remained loyal to Constantius II, yet was drawn into the tug of war between the two. No third country intervened at any point and there was no foreign assistance, and this was the last time the Jews of fourth-century Palestine rose in arms with a whole city as their base.
people: 留下名字的是起義首領朱利安·本·薩巴，以及與他並肩的兄弟利未。朱利安是提比哩亞的拉比兼祭司，出身上層猶太家庭，後世編年稱他為德行深厚的學者，說他被推出來不是因為軍功，而是因為他在社群中的話語權；拉比文獻記下他與利未在該年率眾起事、最終同赴死地的結局，後人因此把那一年記作需要禁食哀悼的年份。皇帝君士坦丁烏斯二世自317年即位，這時在位已三十四年，鎮壓這場叛亂的最高決策出自他的政府：收到東方的消息時，他仍在西線與馬格嫩提烏斯苦戰，只能命令巴勒斯坦總督先行應變，等西線底定才把足夠的部隊與權柄交還東方。爭奪帝位的另一方馬格嫩提烏斯是西羅馬的僭主，351年1月被高盧的軍官與不列顛的駐軍推上皇位；起義者從未直接參與他與君士坦丁烏斯二世之間的戰爭，卻正是這場戰爭構成了他們起兵的直接契機。除起義的兩名首領外，提比哩亞的拉比學者、凱撒利亞的教會以及後世為這段歷史編年的人，構成了這場起義留下的另一批人物。
peopleEn: Two names survive from the rising: the leader Julian son of Sabar and his brother Levi, who stood at his side. Julian was a rabbi and a priest of Tiberias, born into a leading Jewish family, and later chronicles call him a man of deep learning, saying that he was put forward not for any military record but for the authority of his voice within the community; the rabbinic literature records that he and Levi raised the people in that year and met their deaths together, and hence later generations set that year aside as one on which fasting and mourning were required. The emperor Constantius II had reigned since 317 and had been on the throne for thirty-four years; the highest decision to repress the revolt was taken by his government: when the news from the East arrived he was still fighting Magnentius in the West and could only order the governor of Palaestina to hold the line, and it was only once the western front was settled that he sent back to the East troops and authority in sufficient measure. The other claimant to the throne, Magnentius, was the usurper of the western Roman state, raised to the purple in January 351 by officers in Gaul and by the garrison in Britain; the insurgents never took part in his war against Constantius II, yet that very war was the immediate occasion of their rising. Alongside the two chiefs of the revolt, the rabbis of Tiberias, the church of Caesarea and the later chroniclers of this history make up the other company of persons that this rising left behind.
kits: 卡面兵器是埃及月牙劍。它是青銅時代的單刃鉤形砍刀：刃身向內彎曲，砍擊時不必像直刃那樣拔出重來，而是順著鉤勢把刀身拉回來切下去；銅質刀身配木柄，新王國時期的埃及步兵把它列為近身纏鬥的主兵器，與青銅斧、鎚、矛並排在同一套軍械體系之中。要說明的是，月牙劍並未出現在公元351年的巴勒斯坦：這場起義的近身武器，是被徵用為兵器的本地割草鐮刀、修剪刀與短兵，以及從提比哩亞駐軍手中奪得的羅馬短劍、刺劍、標槍與盾牌。功能上最接近的仍是羅馬的直刃刺劍與農用彎刃——起義者沒有制式裝備，靠的正是「不必回抽、一擊即中」的工具邏輯，這一點與月牙劍同源：它們是同一種在缺乏鍛造工藝與兵員補充的環境下，把現成器具改造成砍擊工具的思路。起義者的裝備裡還有石頭、繩索與火油；羅馬方面則是全套制式裝備，短劍與刺劍、重標槍、羅馬圓盾、鎖子甲與分段甲、頭盔，以及在凱撒利亞城牆與城樓之間架設的弩砲。兩者在街巷與城門之間貼身相撞時，決定勝負的往往不是刀刃的形制，而是誰能更快地把人聚集到街上、把武器分發到手上。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Egyptian khopesh. It is a single-edged hooked cutting-sword of the bronze age: the blade curves inward, and in striking it need not be drawn back as a straight blade must be, but is pulled through the cut along the curve of the hook; the bronze blade is socketed on a wooden grip, and in the New Kingdom the Egyptian infantry carried it as a principal close-combat arm, ranked in the same equipment system with the bronze axe, the mace and the spear. It should be said plainly that the khopesh was not present in Palestine in 351 AD: the close-combat weapons of this rising were the local sickles, pruning knives and short blades pressed into service, together with the Roman short swords, thrusting swords, javelins and shields taken from the hands of the Tiberias garrison. The closest functional counterparts remain the straight Roman thrusting sword and the agricultural curved blade, for the insurgents possessed no regulation equipment and relied on exactly the logic of the tool, a stroke that does not need drawing back and that lands on the first pass; in that they share a common ancestry with the khopesh, being two expressions of the same thought, that in a setting short of forging skill and of fresh troops one converts existing tools into cutting weapons. The rebels also had stones, ropes and fire; the Romans had the full regulation set, short swords and thrusting swords, heavy javelins, the round shield, mail and segmentata, helmets, and the bolt-throwers mounted between the walls and the towers of Caesarea. When the two sides met at close quarters in the lanes and at the gates, what decided the issue was seldom the shape of the blade but which side could sooner gather its men into the street and put weapons into their hands.
tactics: 起義的爆發靠三個條件同時成立：帝國內戰抽空了東方，社群的宗教領袖正處威望高峰，而象徵性的攻擊目標近在咫尺。起義從提比哩亞發動——這座由希律·腓力二世於公元21年興建的湖畔城，是加利利地區的重鎮，也是拉比學院所在。義軍先取城內由希律王宮改建的羅馬駐軍堡壘與軍械庫，再沿約旦河谷南下，直撲行省首府凱撒利亞；那裡市場上的皇帝像，是帝國權威在本地最刺眼的一件物件，毀掉它等於把「皇帝在此」的宣告推翻。攻城手法是典型的城鎮街巷戰：窄街、轉角、門樓、屋頂平台，義軍以人數與地形對抗裝備與訓練，沒有攻城塔、沒有撞槌，也不曾圍城，因為他們的目的不是攻下一座城，而是做出一個象徵性的姿態。因此義軍沒有可以固守的城防，也沒有接應的援軍；消息傳開，總督自其他城市調來的部隊一到，局面就逆轉。義軍在戰鬥上只做了兩件事：奪取器械庫取得武器，破壞象徵物宣示不滿，隨即在對方集結完成之前被逐出城市，潰散在鄉間。整體來看，這是一場以城市為核心、以象徵為目標、缺乏持續作戰能力的短促叛亂：它能打亂帝國的時間表，卻無法改變任何一條防線。
tacticsEn: The outbreak of the rising rested on three conditions holding at once: the imperial civil war had drained the East, the religious leadership of the community stood at the height of its prestige, and a symbolic target lay within reach. The rising began at Tiberias, the lakeside city founded by Herod Philip II in 21 AD, the great town of the Galilean region and the seat of the rabbinic academy. The insurgents first took the Roman garrison fortress built out of the Herodian palace together with the armoury inside the town, and then marched south along the valley of the Jordan to strike at Caesarea, the capital of the province; the statue of the emperor in the marketplace there was the most glaring object of imperial authority in the locality, and pulling it down meant overturning the proclamation that the emperor was present. The technique of assault was the ordinary street fighting of a crowded town: narrow lanes, corners, gate towers, roof platforms, in which the insurgents matched numbers and terrain against equipment and training. They had no siege tower, no battering ram, and never formed a blockade, because their aim was not to take a city but to make a symbolic gesture. They therefore had no defences to hold and no relieving force; the news travelled, the governor's troops summoned from other cities arrived, and the situation reversed. In combat the insurgents did only two things: they seized the armoury to obtain weapons, and they destroyed the symbolic object to proclaim their grievance, and then, before the enemy could complete his concentrations, they were driven out of the city and dispersed into the countryside. Viewed whole, this was a short, sudden rebellion centred on a city, aimed at a symbol, and without the means to keep fighting: it could scramble the timetable of the empire, but it could not shift a single line of defence.
data: 這場起義留下的數字很少，可以核對的主要是年表與地理。年表：馬格嫩提烏斯於351年1月被高盧與不列顛的軍隊推舉，與君士坦丁烏斯二世於9月28日在穆爾薩主力戰中交鋒，翌年再戰於小穆爾薩；西線到353年才完全平定，而提比哩亞的起義正落在此後數年，一般記為351年起事、353至354年間被平。距離：提比哩亞位於加利利海西北岸，湖面最深處低於海平面二百一十米；提比哩亞至凱撒利亞為行省內陸路約九十公里，義軍南下走的是約旦河谷與薩福利耶、麥吉多一線。曆法上有一條可以核對的線索：按猶太曆十九年一閏的週期推算，公元351年秋季開始的猶太年是閏年，而公元361年秋季開始的猶太年不是閏年；拉比文獻恰恰把這件事記作一條屬於閏年的法令，因此學者多認為拉比人記憶的正是351年，而不是皇帝陣亡的361年。兵力與損耗方面，史料沒有留下雙方人數的可信記載，沒有陣亡名冊、沒有俘虜數、沒有器械數目；能確定的只是鎮壓由行省自身的部隊完成，帝國中央沒有為此調動野戰大軍。卡面兵器方面，月牙劍屬新王國時期的青銅器，現存博物館實物的總長多在五十至六十公分之間，屬單手握持、以砍劈為主的近身兵器。帝國晚期留下的財政與人口檔案極少，學者只能從提比哩亞的城市規模、會堂與作坊的考古痕跡去推想當時行省的人力，無法給出起義本身的確切人數。
dataEn: Few figures survive for this rising, and what can be checked are chiefly the chronology and the geography. Chronology: Magnentius was proclaimed by the troops of Gaul and Britain in January 351 and fought Constantius II at the battle of Mursa Major on the twenty-eighth of September, with a further engagement at Mursa Minor in the year following; the western front was not settled until 353, and the rising at Tiberias falls in the years just after, being generally reckoned to have begun in 351 and to have been put down between 353 and 354. Distances: Tiberias stands on the north-western shore of the Sea of Galilee, the surface of which lies some two hundred and ten metres below sea level; the inland road from Tiberias to Caesarea runs about ninety kilometres, and the insurgents moved south by the line of the Jordan valley through Saffuriyeh and Megiddo. On the calendar there is one line that can be checked: by the nineteen-year cycle with its seven leap years, the Jewish year beginning in the autumn of 351 CE falls in a leap position, while the Jewish year beginning in the autumn of 361 CE does not; and it is precisely as a regulation belonging to a leap year that the rabbinic literature records this matter, so that most scholars take the memory of the rabbis to be of 351 rather than of 361, the year the emperor died. As to numbers of men and of losses, the sources leave no trustworthy record, no list of casualties, no count of prisoners, no tally of engines; what can be established is that the repression was carried out by the province's own troops, and that the imperial centre did not move a field army for the purpose. As to the weapon on the card, the khopesh is a bronze of the New Kingdom, the surviving museum examples measuring fifty to sixty centimetres in overall length, a one-handed instrument of close combat used chiefly to chop. Fiscal and demographic records from the late empire are exceedingly scarce, and scholars can only infer the manpower of the province from the size of Tiberias and from the archaeological traces of synagogues and workshops; the exact number of the insurgents cannot be given.
cause: 把這場起義的成因拆開，可以看見三層。最下層是宗教改造：四世紀上半葉的巴勒斯坦在教會推動下急速基督教化，殉道者崇拜興起，城市與鄉間建起教會與殉道祠，皇帝崇拜與向皇帝獻祭的義務成為日常稅負之外的第二種重擔；不從這套儀式的人不只承受輿論，還承受行政與經濟上的牽制。第二層是帝國自身的危機：君士坦丁王朝晚期財政吃緊，行省稅負上調，東方各省與中央之間因稅務與軍費的爭議而出現裂痕，地方的社會菁英對中央的索取感到不滿。第三層是直接引爆的機會：351年1月西部的軍隊推翻君士坦丁烏斯二世，帝國東半邊一時只剩象徵性的服從，消息沿軍用道路東傳，普遍被讀成「秩序出現了裂口」；提比哩亞的猶太社群把這個裂口當成窗口。行政上的火種則是凱撒利亞市場上的皇帝像——它要求居民在儀式上向皇帝獻祭，象徵性的拒絕很容易就變成集體性的行動。再加上當時猶太社群內部存在一位有威望、有組織能力的領袖朱利安·本·薩巴，於是當亂局與領袖同時出現，燎原之勢就這樣成形。
causeEn: Taken apart, the causes of this rising reveal three layers. The lowest is religious transformation: in the first half of the fourth century Palestine was Christianised rapidly under the drive of the church, the cult of the martyrs arose, churches and martyr shrines were built in town and country, and the worship of the emperor together with the obligation of offering sacrifice to him became a second weight alongside the ordinary burden of taxation; those who would not take part in that ritual did not merely endure opinion against them but were held in check by administrative and economic pressure. The second layer is the crisis of the empire itself: finances were tight in the late Constantinian period, the fiscal burden on the provinces was raised, and disputes over taxation and military costs opened fissures between the eastern provinces and the centre, so that the local notables grew dissatisfied with what the centre was drawing from them. The third layer is the chance that set the fire alight: in January 351 the troops of the West threw over Constantius II, and for a time the eastern half of the empire had only a symbolic obedience left, the news travelling east along the military roads and being read generally as a sign that order had cracked; the Jewish community of Tiberias took that crack for a window. The administrative spark was the statue of the emperor in the marketplace of Caesarea, which required the inhabitants to offer sacrifice to the emperor in ritual form, and a symbolic refusal could very easily become a collective act. Add to this the fact that within the Jewish community there stood a leader of prestige and of organising ability, Julian son of Sabar, and once the disorder and the leader were present at the same moment, the conflagration took its shape.
impact: 這場起義的直接後果慘酷而短暫，但它在幾個層面留下了痕跡。第一是鎮壓的樣板：總督在皇帝像被毀之後把罪名推向城內的基督徒群體，受損的是教堂與教會的據點，這讓宗教轉向時期的巴勒斯坦多了一層帝國監督的陰影，拉比與教會兩方面的記載從此都帶著戒心。第二是猶太社群集體記憶的形成：後來的編年把這一年記作「帝王崩年」，規定該年不照常吃逾越節的羔羊，另有說法指該年有人慘死於山野；那段記載正是拉比文獻裡朱利安與利未兄弟的來歷，說明這場起義在教義上被記成一場需要哀悼的災難。第三是四世紀巴勒斯坦猶太社群的走向：舊式的武裝起義在提比哩亞這次之後沒有再成功過，直到五世紀初的西頓之戰被羅馬與波斯聯軍壓碎；自此猶太社群的韌性主要體現在拉比學術、拉比禮拜與家庭和社群的延續上，而不再體現在城市義軍上。第四是帝國的教訓：任何內戰都可能在行省裡製造出真空，而一次針對象徵物的集體襲擊足以讓遠方的皇帝無法確定自己的統治是否仍然成立，這種不確定性本身就成為羅馬晚期行省治理的長期成本。
impactEn: The immediate consequences of this rising were harsh and short-lived, but it left traces on several levels. First, it set a pattern for repression: after the statue of the emperor was pulled down the governor turned the blame on the Christian community within the city, and what suffered were the churches and the strongholds of the church, so that Palestine in the years of the religious turn acquired an additional shadow of imperial supervision, and the accounts of both rabbis and churchmen thereafter are written with caution. Second, it formed part of the collective memory of the Jewish community: later chronicles set that year apart as the year in which the emperor died, laying down that the Passover lamb was not to be eaten in the ordinary way in that year, and in another version saying that men perished in the wild in that year; that very notice is the source of Julian and his brother Levi in the rabbinic literature, showing that the rising was entered in the tradition as a catastrophe requiring mourning. Third, it set the direction of the Jewish community of fourth-century Palestine: the old style of armed insurrection did not succeed again after Tiberias, until it was crushed at the battle of Sittacene in the early fifth century by the allied Roman and Persian armies; from then on the resilience of the community was expressed in rabbinic learning, in the rabbinic synagogue and in the continuity of family and community, and no longer in the civic armed rising. Fourth, it taught the empire a lesson: any civil war may open a vacuum in a province, and a collective blow struck at a symbol may be enough to leave the emperor in far-off Rome unable to be sure that his rule still held, and that uncertainty itself became a permanent cost of provincial government in the late Roman world.
result: 結局是鎮壓：起義在提比哩亞爆發後不足數年即被壓平。朱利安·本·薩巴與利未兄弟在事件中身亡，後世編年記下二人被處決，提比哩亞城在戰事中遭到焚掠，部分城區成為廢墟，城市的重建與會堂的修復在隨後數十年裡才完成；教長駐節與拉比學院的制度雖然受到衝擊，本身卻得以延續，行省的稅務與軍務秩序很快恢復。結果沒有改變任何一條長線：皇帝崇拜的儀式照舊在凱撒利亞舉行，基督教化照舊推進，猶太社群既沒有得到自治，也沒有得到特權，「帝王崩年」的禁食成為一段儀式性的記憶。從戰略上看，失敗的原因相當清楚：目標是象徵而不是地盤，缺少時間把一次突發轉成制度，缺少與鄉間的連結，缺少外邦支援，而在消滅西線的馬格嫩提烏斯之後，帝國迅速把注意力與兵力調回東方。從歷史的長視角看，這是四世紀羅馬巴勒斯坦的猶太人最後一次大規模的武力嘗試，此後猶太人的歷史在帝國框架之內轉為學術、律法與家庭生命的延續，直到五世紀末的失陷與七世紀的伊斯蘭征服帶來新的斷裂。
resultEn: The outcome was repression: the rising was put down within a few years of breaking out at Tiberias. Julian son of Sabar and his brother Levi lost their lives in it, later chronicles recording that the two were executed, and Tiberias was sacked and burned in the fighting, part of the town lying in ruins, with the rebuilding of the city and the repair of its synagogue completed only over the following decades; the institutions of the patriarchal residence and of the rabbinic academy, though shaken, survived, and the fiscal and military order of the province was quickly restored. Nothing on any long line was changed: the rites of the imperial cult went on being performed at Caesarea, the Christianisation of the province went on advancing, the Jewish community won neither autonomy nor privilege, and the fast kept for the year the emperor died remained a piece of ritual memory. Viewed strategically, the reasons for the failure are clear enough: the object was a symbol rather than territory, there was no time to convert a sudden outbreak into an institution, no link to the countryside, no foreign assistance, and once Magnentius had been destroyed in the West the empire quickly turned its attention and its troops back to the East. Viewed from the long perspective of history, this was the last large armed attempt of the Jews of Roman Palestine in the fourth century, after which the history of the Jews within the imperial framework turned into the continuity of learning, law and domestic life, until the loss of the country in the late fifth century and the Islamic conquest of the seventh brought a new rupture.
